Training

Two strength days built for marathon training — plus three runs and tennis.
✓ Saved automatically
Make it an app: in Safari, tap the Share button, then Add to Home Screen. It then opens full-screen with its own icon and saves your progress automatically on this phone.
Do this before both strength days. ~5–8 min. It raises your heart rate and rehearses the day's movements so the right muscles are ready before you load them.
Jumping Jacks / High Knees~2 min
Easy, steady pace just to raise your heart rate and get warm. Mix the two if you like. Finish warm, not tired.
Bodyweight Squats10 reps
Sit hips down and back, chest tall, knees over toes.
Leg Swings10 / leg
Hold a wall for balance. Swing one leg forward and back in a controlled arc, then switch. Loosens the hips, hamstrings and glutes through a running range of motion.
Arm Circles10 + 10
Slow, full circles. Warms the shoulders.
First exercise — light set1 × 8
One light set of the day's first move to bridge into working sets.
Why these exercises: strength work is the best protection against running injuries, and heavy lifting improves running economy by roughly 2–8% — the same pace costs less oxygen. The calf and glute work matters most: the calves and Achilles take the heaviest load in running, and the glutes are what stop your hips dropping late in a long run.
Between sets90s squat & deadlift · 60s the rest.
Finding weightLast 2 reps hard but clean = right. 3+ in the tank = go heavier.
Save timeSuperset the calf raises with the core move — you rest anyway.
Progress: heavy and low-rep, not high-rep. When the top of the rep range stops feeling hard, add weight and drop back to the bottom of the range. Aim to add load every 2–3 weeks. Calves first: start with bodyweight only for a week or two, then add a dumbbell.
Between sets90s split squat & hip thrust · 60s the rest.
Single-sideOne side, then the other, then rest before the next set.
Day B emphasis: single-leg drive and the soleus. Running is a long series of one-legged hops, so single-leg strength carries over far better than two-legged lifting.
Week: Mon Strength A · Tue easy run · Wed Strength B · Thu rest or easy bike · Fri rest · Sat long run · Sun easy run on tired legs. Never lift heavy the day before the long Saturday run.
Just type — it saves itself. Each week, fill in the weight and reps you hit. A 🔶 PB tag appears when you beat your previous best weight on a move.
